Ethan — adding SRE/SE context. I ran the sample through our load synth:

Summary (quantized 16B):
- H100 equivalent (our benchmark): 2.1k tokens/sec per GPU (short context median workload)
- A100 equivalent: ~1.5k tokens/sec per GPU
- Long-context (2k window) effective tokens/sec drops to ~950 tps on H100 due to KV overhead

SLO fit guidance: to hit 99th <= 450ms with a 25% safety buffer for spike absorption, baseline slab = 12 H100 GPUs. That assumes balanced autoscaling in the Dedicated pool and prefix caching for session reuse. Conservative (30% headroom) = 16 H100s; aggressive (minimal buffer) = 9–10 H100s.

Notes on fallbacks: recommend a fallback policy that routes to a smaller quantized variant (14B int8) under sustained capacity pressure; that drops quality marginally but keeps latency predictable. Also suggest a burst tranche of shared capacity (3–4 GPUs) in case of anomalous traffic.

— Ben

Folks — I calculated the end-to-end tokens/sec math and headroom assumptions; dropping into plain steps so procurement can follow: 

1) Workload split (from sample): 72% short (<=512), 28% long (>=2k).
2) Effective tps per GPU (median, H100): short = 2,100 tps; long = 950 tps.
3) Weighted effective tps per GPU = 0.72*2100 + 0.28*950 = 1,742 tps.
4) Peak demand target they specified = 12,000 tps sustained (short windows).
5) Base GPUs required = ceil(12,000 / 1,742) = 7 GPUs.

Headroom & SLO considerations:
- Latency SLO (99th <= 450ms) requires nonlinearity headroom for queuing; apply a 1.7x safety multiplier to the base slab to preserve tail latency under bursty arrivals and batching jitter.
- Recommended committed slab = 7 * 1.7 = 11.9 -> round to 12 GPUs (H100-equivalent).
- Conservative committed slab (30% extra) = 16 GPUs; minimal viable commit (no headroom) = 8 GPUs.

Operational notes:
- Prefill KV cache for returning sessions reduces long-request penalty by ~25% — if Heliograph can ensure session affinity we can drop required GPUs by ~1–2 on baseline.
- Quantization: int8 variants increase per-GPU tps by ~20% but test coverage required for quality parity.
- Fallback plan: automatic downgrade to 14B-int8 variant + redirect to hot shared burst pool when sustained utilization >85% for more than 90s.

I've attached the brief math workbook and a short scenario table showing latency vs utilization curves. Happy to discuss the queuing model if procurement wants the derivation.

Attachments: heliograph-math-model.xlsx
